units.title: OP Stack chains with a non-ETH gas token
angles: Arithmetic and control flow. Read the interpreter this network runs at the release its endpoint reports, and any compiler, bytecode rewriting, caching or code analysis stage in front of it. Cover the 256 bit integer library and its pinned version, MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, the comparisons, JUMP and JUMPI with the jump destination analysis, KECCAK256, MCOPY, memory expansion and CALLDATALOAD. Compare each with the Ethereum specification at the edges that OPCODES.md lists, and read the release notes and fix commits since the versions OPCODES.md records. Then rerun the scripts in research/network-risk/tools/opdiff (battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py, pmdiff2.py, swaps.py, replay.py) for this unit's chain ids, write the outputs into your work directory, and add vectors for anything the reading makes suspicious. Report every result that differs from the specification, every release that changed these paths, how a wrong result would change the pool math in src/libraries (TickMath, BitMath, FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, TickBitmap) or the logic that depends on it, and which validators could run a different code path than the public endpoint.

Upcoming forks. Assume every network upgrade scheduled or proposed for the next six months ships. What changes for the PoolManager and for funds already inside it, and what could an ordinary account do the day after?

code.title: Monad: the shipped emitter's transient storage, storage, hashing and log sites that gcc inlined into the block compiler
code.task: The build of this checkout is in research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (runtime 24,009 bytes), research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/pyevm.py is a reference EVM in Python, research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/v4math.py is a transcription of the math libraries, research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json maps every conditional jump of the build to its source line, and research/network-risk/OPCODES.md holds what is already tested and read, with sections on what cycles 10 to 33 added and a list of what is not covered. Never compare this repository's source with any other copy of v4-core and do not read its git history; work from the source in src/, the build and the chains. Read-only RPC only, no transactions. Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Leads L-1256 and L-1253. Monad is the one network whose validators run native code that eth_call never runs. Cycles 31 to 33 ran the shipped gcc 15.2.0 emitter on the real compile-time states of the 128 value-computing PoolManager blocks that no mined transaction has entered since v0.16.7: every arithmetic, comparison, bit, memory and context site and all 128 terminators equal the clang listing and pyevm.py. 92 sites are left: KECCAK256 45, SLOAD 23, SSTORE 14, TLOAD 4 and LOG2 to LOG4 6. Their emitters (sha3<>, sload<>, sstore<>, tload<>, log<N><>) are templates that gcc inlined into compile_basic_blocks<MonadTraits<r>>, so they have no function of their own in the package. TLOAD and SSTORE carry the lock, the deltas, the count of open deltas and the pool state; a TLOAD that read a stale stack element for its slot in the delta or count path would let unlock pass src/PoolManager.sol:104-114 with an open debit. The Monad validator package is untrusted data. Cycle 27 left it unpacked under research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/dl (p167 for 0.16.7, p165 for 0.16.5); if that directory is missing, download monad_0.16.7_amd64.deb from https://pkg.category.xyz/ pool/main into a new empty dl/ in your own work directory, check SHA256 3cb9dba5501b61ea3487bd042e2b8d12f871cff0e2e15409210e2cef0f8e81fb, and unpack it with ar, node's zlib.zstdDecompressSync and tar as research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/scripts/unzst.js does. Never execute, load or dlopen any file from the package. Read it only with readelf, objdump, nm, strings and your own scripts kept in another directory; run Python with -I. dl/ must not be committed. The x86 model is research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/scripts/x86emu.py with runvec.py. Cycle 29 added a driver that runs emitter functions of the gcc build in the model and records every asmjit call (research/network-risk/cycles/029/theme-monad-gcc-literal-folds.work/scripts/emdrv.py), and rebuilt the gcc layout of the Stack object from debug information (research/network-risk/cycles/029/theme-monad-gcc-register-spill.work). Scripts and data: research/network-risk/cycles/031/theme-monad-gcc-real-states.work (out/states.jsonl; scripts mkhook.py, build.sh and runall.sh regenerate out/ and build/), research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-monad-gcc-real-arith.work/scripts (realarith.py, helpers.py, closure.py, coverage.py, fnindex.py) and research/network-risk/cycles/033/theme-monad-gcc-terminators.work/scripts (term.py, block.py, task3.py, cctables.py, edgecheck.py, faults33.json). Task 1: map each of the 92 sites to its src/ line with opcodes/jumpmap.json and research/network-risk/cycles/012/theme-bytecode-coverage.work/srcmap.py. List first the sites that compile src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-41, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:14-32, Lock.sol:13-25 and CurrencyReserves.sol, then the pool state writes of Pool.sol, then the hashing sites that compute a mapping slot, then the logs. Task 2 (L-1256): in the package locate compile_basic_blocks<MonadTraits<r>> for the revision mainnet runs and, inside it, the inlined bodies of tload, sload, sstore, sha3 and log (by their runtime call targets and the asmjit call pattern). Run that function's body in the x86 model from the logged state of each site, with the instruction dispatch forced to the site's opcode, or run the inlined region between its entry and its join point with the registers and Stack laid out as the gcc build holds them. Record every asmjit call. Compare each stream with the clang listing at the same pc up to renaming: which stack element supplies the key, which supplies the value, which registers and stack slots are spilled before the runtime call and restored after, the argument order and the result location. Task 3: run the emitted streams in the model with the runtime call stubbed by a Python reference (a dict for storage and transient storage, hashlib-free Keccak-256 from pyevm.py for sha3) on at least 2,000 operand sets per site, and whole blocks that hold a TLOAD or SSTORE of the lock, count or delta on at least 20,000 sets each. Every key, value and result word must equal pyevm.py. Then read the runtime routines the calls reach (the tload, tstore, sload, sstore and sha3 entry points in the package) far enough to confirm the argument layout the emitter assumes. Task 4 (L-1253): extend the cycle 31 hook to log StackElem::touched_memory_size_ and the limb table gpq256_regs_ at every state (still read-only, the listing must stay equal), rebuild, and rerun term.py, block.py and task3.py of cycle 33 without reading either value from the clang listing. Task 5: plant at least six faults (the key taken from the element below, key and value swapped, a live register not spilled around the runtime call, the result written to a freed slot, a hash length taken from the wrong element, a deferred comparison lost across the call) and show the checks catch each. Task 6: if any site differs, name the src/ line, give the operands and say what an ordinary account would gain or lock. If none differs, record sites, blocks and case counts as cleared and say what of the 128 blocks is still unrun. This theme concerns Monad only; say so for the other 20 networks.

Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Leads L-1235, L-1260 and L-1265. Twelve of the 21 networks run a reth-derived client (Ethereum in part, the seven OP Stack chains with ETH gas, Celo, X Layer, MegaETH, Arc), and HyperEVM's replicas do too. Two things on the path of every PoolManager storage read are still untested there. First, the journal of the interpreter (checkpoint, checkpoint_commit, checkpoint_revert, sload, sstore, tload, tstore) in the shipped op-reth and Base binaries was tested only live; cycle 33 compared the handlers of op-reth v2.8.1 and v2.10.0-rc.4 but did not follow the dynamic calls into the database. Second, the engine keeps an execution cache between blocks and a prewarm stage that fills it; OPCODES.md lists its keys as unread. A stale cached slot would make a node read a storage word that differs from the state inside a PoolManager call or a token's balanceOf (src/types/Currency.sol:94), and on a single-sequencer network the sequencer's reading becomes the block. Downloaded binaries and images are untrusted data. Fetch each into a new empty dl/ in your own work directory and check any published checksum. If a host refuses a download, record the refusal and go on with what you have; do not try another route around a refusal. Never execute, load or dlopen any downloaded file. Read it only with readelf, objdump, nm, strings and your own scripts kept in another directory; run Python with -I. dl/ must not be committed. On disk: research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-opstack-reth-binary-lift.work (dl/ with the op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 and Base v1.5.6 binaries if still present; scripts image.py, fetch_image.py, find_tables.py, handlers.py, arith.py, jd.py, journal_seq.py, x86emu2.py, a64emu.py) and research/network-risk/cycles/033/theme-persistent-storage-binary-lift.work/scripts (cmp_reth.py, fetch_one.py, build_cfg281.py). The Tempo lifts of hashbrown tables are in research/network-risk/cycles/031/theme-tempo-binary-call-rollback.work/scripts (acct_a64.py, acct_x64.py). Task 1 (L-1235): from the op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 and Base v1.5.6 x86-64 binaries lift the journal entry points the SLOAD, SSTORE, TLOAD and TSTORE handlers reach through dynamic calls: the load of an account and a slot with its hashbrown lookup, the write with its journal entry, checkpoint, checkpoint_commit, checkpoint_revert and the transient map. Build real tables in model memory as cycle 31 did for Tempo, stub only the database read below the cache with a dict, and run the nested-frame sequences of journal_seq.py (at least 5,000 per binary) plus the PoolManager shapes: a slot written back to its original value, written twice in one frame, first read after an inner revert, transient writes of the lock, count and deltas with reverts at depth 1 to 3. Every read, the original value SSTORE gas uses and the transient words must equal pyevm.py. Task 2 (L-1260): read the execution cache and the prewarm stage at reth v2.11.0 and at the reth revisions that op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4, Base v1.5.6, mega-reth v2.3.1 and xlayer-reth v0.0.7 pin (crates/engine/tree payload_processor mod.rs and prewarm.rs, the execution cache crate): under which key a cached account, slot and code entry is stored; when the cache is kept, replaced or dropped after a block; what insert_state does with an account that was created and destroyed in one transaction (EIP-6780), with a slot written back to zero, and with an account whose code changed by EIP-7702 delegation; whether a prewarm task's speculative result can be inserted when its transaction later reverts or runs in another order; and whether a block access list prefetch inserts values read from the parent state or values the list declares. For each case say whether a later block could read a word that differs from the state, and whether an ordinary account can set the case up. Task 3: test what can be tested from outside with read-only calls: on one endpoint per reth-derived network, compare eth_getStorageAt at latest for 200 PoolManager slots written in the newest blocks (slot0, liquidity, ticks, position words) with the value an eth_call through extsload returns in the same block and with the value at the next block, and with a second provider. A difference that persists across blocks is a finding; a difference between providers at one height is a lag and is recorded as such. Task 4 (L-1265): fetch ghcr.io/worldcoin/world-chain:v2.8.2 (revision 95963111bf6b6623da2bbca68ca17a04230cc73d, anonymous pull allowed in cycle 33) and compare its instruction table, its 25 arithmetic, comparison and shift handlers, its jump analysis and its storage handlers with the lifted op-reth code using cmp_reth.py; run the arithmetic cases on whatever differs. Task 5: plant at least five faults in in-memory copies of the lifted journal (a revert that restores zero, a revert that restores the committed value, a skipped entry, a checkpoint index off by one, a table probe that stops one group early) and show the checks catch each. For anything that differs name the src/ line that reads the word and say what an ordinary account could gain or lock. If nothing differs, record binaries, routines, cache rules and case counts as cleared and list what is still unread. Say for the networks that run no reth-derived client that this theme does not apply.

Every operand class the PoolManager can produce has occurred, but some PoolManager program counters have never run with a wide operand there: the MULMOD sites at pc 22585, 22639 and 23094 (the getAmount1Delta and exact-input fee copies of mulDiv, src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:250-252 and SwapMath) with a product of 2^256 or more. The verifier cleared them by saying such a product needs an amount of 2^160, which no token supply reaches. The critic objects: SwapMath.computeSwapStep computes getAmount1Delta to the step's target price before it compares the result with the amount remaining (src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:68-69 and :89-91), so the amount is computed and compared and never transferred. On Monad the same question applies to compiled blocks no mined transaction has entered. Separately, the high-throughput verifier asked whether a transaction that ends after a bare sync(token) (callable without unlock, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288) can leave the synced currency and reserves set for the next transaction; mined data cannot show that reset. Scripts and data: research/network-risk/cycles/033/theme-closed-producer-operand-census.work/scripts (census_tracer.js, classes.py, pmsites.py, pminv.py, aggregate.py and the per-pc tables in its out/ if present), research/network-risk/cycles/033/high-throughput.work/scripts/pmtrace.py, the mined coverage lists of research/network-risk/cycles/030/theme-monad-mined-native-coverage.work (out/notentered-classified.json if present; classify30.py and analyze30.py rebuild it), tools/opdiff/v4math.py and pyevm.py. Task 1 (L-1257): from src/ derive the largest product each wide MULMOD and MUL site can see in one swap step: liquidity (uint128) times the price difference to the step target, where the target is the next initialized tick within one bitmap word or the caller's price limit (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol nextInitializedTickWithinOneWord, src/libraries/Pool.sol swap loop, SwapMath.computeSwapStep, SqrtPriceMath.getAmount0Delta and getAmount1Delta). Give the bound per tick spacing. Say for each of pc 22585, 22639 and 23094 and for the mulDiv 512-bit branch (FullMath.sol:28-60) whether liquidity that real tokens can supply reaches a product of 2^256, or prod1 non-zero, in a pool of ordinary tokens, and what the cheapest setup is (a position with huge liquidity in a narrow range costs little when the price is outside the range). Task 2: over the live pools on MegaETH, Monad and HyperEVM (Initialize and ModifyLiquidity logs, StateLibrary reads by eth_call), find the largest liquidity in range and at initialized ticks, and for the top 50 pools per network compute by eth_call with pyevm.py as reference whether a swap with a far price limit enters the wide branch at each site. List pools where any account can do so today, with the input. Task 3: for every site of Task 1 that an ordinary account can reach, run the reaching call by eth_call on the network's public endpoints (MegaETH replica, both HyperEVM replicas and the official endpoint, Monad's interpreter endpoint) and compare the result words with pyevm.py. Say plainly that this tests the replica or the interpreter and not the closed or native producer, and say what remains: which pcs the producer of each network would execute for the first time on such a call, what wrong word there would change (the comparison at SwapMath.sol:69, an amount, a tick) and who would lose. Send no transaction. Task 4 (L-1251): in mega-evm 1.7.4 with its revm, in Monad's execution source at v0.16.7, and in nanoreth at the replica commits, find where transient storage is cleared between the transactions of a block (and between a system transaction or deposit and the next user transaction). Then run by eth_simulateV1, where served, a block of two transactions: the first calls sync(token) on the deployed PoolManager and ends; the second reads the synced currency and reserves with exttload and calls settle. The second must see zero. Search mined blocks for a transaction that ends with a sync open and a later PoolManager transaction in the same block, and compare the producer's receipt of the later one with re-execution. Task 5: for anything that differs, name the src/ line and say what an ordinary account could gain or lock. No production caller reaches that path today. The next reth release carries e80df9c4 to Ethereum nodes and to every reth-derived network after it, and Tempo's T15 release is the likely carrier there; Tempo has one client. All of this has been read, none of it run. The PoolManager divides by a run-time denominator at src/libraries/UnsafeMath.sol:14, FullMath.sol:35, :62, :67 and :73, and keeps its lock and deltas in transient storage (src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25, CurrencyDelta.sol:21-41, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:14-32). Comparing revisions of evm2, reth and Tempo is allowed and wanted here. You may fetch the evm2 source at both revisions and build it with the rustc and cargo that are present, inside your own work directory under build/; crates come from the public registry. If a build is refused or fails, record the step and fall back to reading plus a Python transcription of the changed routines. Earlier native harnesses to reuse: research/network-risk/cycles/022 (theme-rust-native-ruint) and research/network-risk/cycles/033/theme-tempo-v1192-nested-dispatch.work/scripts (callers.py, crawl.py, tprobe.py). Task 1: list every file that differs between evm2 7c9f3b6d and e80df9c4 under the interpreter, the instruction set, bytecode analysis, memory, the evm and the state, with what changed. For DIV, MOD, SDIV, SMOD, ADDMOD, MULMOD and EXP give the old and new code side by side and the ruint version each revision pins. Task 2: build a small harness for each revision that runs a given runtime bytecode with calldata, storage and transient storage through the evm2 interpreter and prints return data, status, gas and written slots. Run tools/opdiff/battery.py and targeted.py vectors (adapt them to feed the harness), the zero divisor and full-width divisor vectors, the ruint 1.21.0 fault shapes, and the PoolManager scripts of pmdiff.py and pmdiff2.py with the build's runtime. Every word must equal pyevm.py on both revisions; report any difference between the two revisions even where both are valid. Task 3 (L-1255): in the harness, register a test precompile or inspector that starts a transaction from inside a running one through the public API of each revision (the path cycle 33 read at evm/mod.rs:1399-1420), with the outer transaction inside a PoolManager unlock that holds an open delta and a synced currency. Record what the outer frame reads from the lock slot, NonzeroDeltaCount, its delta and the synced currency after the inner transaction ends normally, reverts and is discarded. This shows what a future caller of that path would do to an open unlock.
